### Position read
The opponent advanced Red from (0,3) to center (3,3). We moved Blue from (4,7) to the lower-right center (4,4). All losses remain zero.

### Our plan
Contest center immediately. If (4,3) remains open on Green’s turn, strongly consider Green (4,0)->(4,3), giving us both lower central squares. Otherwise develop Green to block the opponent’s center majority and build same-color sandwich flanks. Keep Blue (4,4) unless a concrete tactical move is stronger.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent opened with an immediate central occupation, suggesting a center-focused plan.

### Lessons
Red at (3,3) makes (3,2) and (3,4) tactically dangerous for Blue: Red may land on the opposite side and sandwich-capture. Teammate colors never form capture flanks, and friendly pieces can be captured inside mixed sandwich lines.

### Position read
The opponent holds (3,3) with Red and (4,3) with Yellow; we hold (4,4) with Blue. Green has advanced to (4,2), beside Yellow, with all losses still zero. The opponent controls two of four center squares but cannot complete center occupation while our Blue remains at (4,4).

### Our plan
Keep Blue (4,4) unless moving it enables a concrete tactic or is necessary to avoid capture. Use Green (4,2) as a same-color sandwich anchor: after safely clearing Blue from (4,4), seek to bring another Green onto (4,4) vertically and capture Yellow at (4,3). Contest (3,4) with Blue if practical, while watching for Red’s likely arrival there.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent is pursuing rapid center occupation with both colors.

### Lessons
Green (4,2) and Blue (4,4) do not sandwich Yellow because teammate colors cannot flank together. Moving into a sandwich is safe; only a move by the potential capturer triggers captures.

### Position read
All losses remain zero. The opponent holds center squares (3,3) with Red and (4,3) with Yellow; our Blue has withdrawn from (4,4) to (5,4), while Green remains at (4,2). Blue had to leave (4,4) because Yellow could land at (4,5) and sandwich it against Yellow (4,3).

### Our plan
Use Blue (5,4) as a vertical sandwich anchor. If the opponent occupies (4,4), Blue may capture from (3,4); if Red also stacks at (3,4), Blue may be able to land at (2,4) and capture the whole intervening chain. Keep contesting column 4 and avoid allowing all four center squares to remain opponent-occupied. Green should improve access toward the center while preserving (4,2) as a possible horizontal anchor.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent is pursuing rapid center occupation and has advanced Red to (2,4), likely to support entry into (3,4).

### Lessons
Same-color anchors are tactically valuable even outside the center. Before occupying a center square, check whether the opponent can land beyond it using an existing same-color piece as the far flank.

### Position read
All losses remain zero. The opponent occupies central (3,3), with another piece at (4,3) and support at (2,4) and (6,4). We have pieces at (5,4) and now (5,2). Moving from (4,2) avoided an immediate sandwich by an opponent landing at (4,1) against the opponent anchor at (4,3).

### Our plan
On our next turn, contest the center according to the opponent's move. A piece on (3,7) can reach (3,4), while the piece on (5,4) can reach (4,4) if clear. Prefer the square that cannot immediately be sandwiched; occupying (3,4) is vulnerable to an opponent landing at (3,5) against the anchor at (3,3). Keep (5,4) as a vertical tactical anchor and develop (5,2) toward useful central lanes.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent is pursuing fast center occupation and uses same-color anchors to create sandwich threats.

### Lessons
Before leaving a piece adjacent to an opponent, check whether that opponent can land on the opposite side using an existing same-color anchor. Center occupation must also be tested for an immediate sandwich reply.

### Position read
All losses are zero. The opponent holds three central squares: Red at (3,3),(3,4) and Yellow at (4,3). We have just moved Blue from (5,4) to the final center square (4,4), preventing an immediate center victory. Blue at (4,4) is vulnerable to Yellow moving (7,5)->(4,5), sandwiching it against Yellow at (4,3).

### Our plan
If Yellow captures at (4,4), use the Green turn to seek a forcing counterattack or securely recontest the center. Preserve useful Green pieces at (5,2) and the left edge while developing toward central approach squares. Blue’s pieces on column 7 can later attack row 3, but Red’s adjacent pair currently blocks direct penetration.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent is aggressively assembling center occupation and maintaining same-color anchors for sandwich tactics. Expect the available Yellow sandwich on Blue at (4,4).

### Lessons
When three center squares are already held, stopping immediate center completion overrides ordinary development. A forced blocker can buy a tempo even when it is capturable; evaluate the opponent’s landing square for a counterattack on the following allied turn.

### Position read
Losses: we have lost one Blue; all others are at zero. The opponent occupies (3,3),(3,4),(4,3), while (4,4) is empty after Yellow captured our blocker. Green moved from (5,2) to (4,2), adjacent to the central Yellow. Red can currently move (3,4)->(4,4) and complete center occupation; no legal Green move this turn could occupy (4,4) or capture a central piece.

### Our plan
If the opponent misses the immediate center win, contest (4,4) at the first opportunity and exploit Green’s pressure from (4,2). Blue should seek direct central access while avoiding another easy Yellow sandwich.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent prioritizes center occupation and accurately used the Yellow anchor at (4,3) to sandwich our Blue blocker.

### Lessons
Before using a sacrificial center blocker, verify whether its capture leaves the vacated center square immediately reachable by another opponent color. Central threats must be assessed across both opposing turns.

### Position read
Losses: we have lost one Blue; all others remain at zero. The opponent still controls three center squares: Red at (3,3),(3,4) and Yellow at (4,3). Yellow at (4,5) can move directly to empty (4,4) on the next turn, completing center occupation. Blue has no legal move that reaches (4,4), captures a central piece, or otherwise prevents that finish. Blue moved (3,7)->(3,5), with no capture.

### Our plan
The position is tactically lost if the opponent sees (4,5)->(4,4). If that win is missed, use Blue at (3,5) as a flank: placing Blue at (5,5), or otherwise arranging the opposite endpoint, can sandwich the Yellow on (4,5). Green must contest (4,4) or attack the center immediately at its next opportunity.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent has strongly prioritized the center, but Red unexpectedly declined an available center-completing move on the previous turn.

### Lessons
When three enemy team pieces occupy the center, every off-center enemy piece aligned with the fourth square must be treated as an immediate winning mover. Verify whether the acting color can occupy the gap before considering longer-term tactics.
